info.name: Traffic Monitoring API
info.description:
**Sprint 3 — Traffic Monitoring Dashboard | API Test Suite**_51 test cases (TC00–TC50) | 6 folders | Built against actual source code_

---

**Folder 0 — Unauthenticated Guard (TC00–TC01)**  
Verifies that both the GET history and POST create endpoints reject requests with no token, returning 401 before any business logic runs, TC50 confirms the alerts endpoint also enforces authentication, returning 401 with no token.

**Folder 1 — Authentication (TC02)**  
Confirms the login endpoint returns 200, that the response body carries a valid JWT (verified as 3-segment dot-separated string), and that the token is chained into the environment for all downstream requests.

**Folder 2 — Data Ingestion & Validation — POST (TC03–TC22)**  
TC03 covers the happy-path creation and validates the full response schema (UUID id, echoed fields, float precision with closeTo). TC04–TC07 probe the four exact boundary values permitted by the annotations: trafficDensity=0, trafficDensity=500, avgSpeed=0.0, avgSpeed=200.0 — all must return 201. TC08–TC12 cross each constraint in the opposite direction (density > 500, density < 0, speed < 0, speed > 200, invalid enum) expecting 400. TC13–TC19 test missing and null required fields driven by @NotBlank, @Size(max=50), and @NotNull annotations. TC20–TC22 send the wrong JSON type for numeric and date fields (string where int/float/LocalDateTime is expected), confirming Spring's deserialization rejects them with 400.

**Folder 3 — Dashboard & Filtering — GET (TC23–TC41)**  
TC23 validates the real response envelope shape: a wrapper object with a `data` array and a `total` integer, not a plain array — with per-record type checks on all six dashboard fields. TC24–TC28 cover the limit parameter: negative and zero values silently default to 10 (not a 400), a valid custom limit is respected, and non-numeric strings like `abc` and `3abc` are rejected. TC29–TC31 test congestionLevel filtering including a valid match, an unknown enum value (400), and lowercase input (400, confirming case-sensitivity). TC32–TC37 cover date range filtering: both bounds together, each bound independently, malformed date strings (400), and a valid future range that returns an empty result. TC38–TC41 target the location filter specifically, confirming it uses exact match (cb.equal, not LIKE): a partial string returns an empty array, a blank value is silently ignored, and an unknown location returns 200 with an empty data array rather than a 404.

**Folder 4 — Sorting (TC42–TC47)**  
TC42–TC45 verify all four meaningful sort combinations: avgSpeed ascending, trafficDensity descending, timestamp descending (most recent first), and timestamp ascending (oldest first), each asserting the ordering holds across consecutive pairs. TC46–TC47 confirm the silent-fallback behavior encoded in the service: an unrecognised sortDir defaults to descending and an unrecognised sortBy defaults to timestamp, neither returning a 400.

**Folder 5 — Alert Trigger Verification (TC48–TC50)**  
TC48 POSTs a reading that violates both configured thresholds (trafficDensity=500, avgSpeed=5.0, congestionLevel=SEVERE), confirms 201 and validates the saved record fields. TC49 then hits GET /api/alerts and asserts at least one alert exists, that it carries the expected schema fields (id, timestamp, type referencing TRAFFIC), and that no sensitive data is leaked.
